problem_and_intended_users_defined.rationale: P-054 addresses a narrow maintainer/new-contributor problem: determine whether a checkout exposes a bounded onboarding baseline and explain gaps without requiring GitHub API credentials or mutation authority.

public_repository_or_distribution_surfac.rationale: The product is public as source, a reusable composite Action and the non-draft v0.9.1 release.

explicit_open_source_license.rationale: The public repository carries the MIT License covering the P-054 implementation.

complete_readme.rationale: Product documentation covers purpose, CLI/Action usage, status semantics, upstream boundary, architecture, privacy/security, accessibility/localization, recovery, release history and limitations.

beginner_start_here_path.rationale: A dedicated beginner path explains what is checked, how to run it, how to interpret results, privacy, recovery and why v0.9.0 is not completion evidence.

engineering_or_architecture_documentatio.rationale: The engineering path documents the GitHub authority boundary, data flow, threat model, bounded file rules, hard-false claims, language isolation, acceptance strategy and no-network/no-mutation architecture.

reproducible_installation_or_use_instruc.rationale: Consumers can run the dependency-light Python CLI or invoke the exact released @v0.9.1 composite Action; repeated released-ref execution verifies deterministic evidence for the same language/input.

safety_scope_and_limitations.rationale: The product explicitly excludes API/server verification, policy correctness, issue/comment/label/invite mutation, contributor trust decisions, repository code execution, WCAG conformance and contributor-experience guarantees.

recovery_or_rollback_guidance_for_mutati.rationale: P-054 is non-mutating; recovery is deletion of runner-temporary/external outputs and rerun. Any later maintainer edits to community-health files remain ordinary Git-reviewed changes with standard revert.

tests_and_ci.rationale: Adversarial tests and hosted acceptance cover path/symlink/size/output containment, missing/gap semantics, deterministic evidence, EN/ES truth consistency, same-job multilingual output isolation, exact-source release control and released-ref consumer immutability.

security_and_privacy_review.rationale: The review covers no token/API/network authority, no repository code execution or mutation, bounded known paths, symlink/size/output refusal, privacy-safe public support and explicit non-claims.

accessibility_review.rationale: The interface is text-first JSON/Markdown with explicit headings and no color-only semantics. This applicability review does not claim WCAG conformance or human assistive-technology acceptance.

multilingual_path_considered.rationale: English and Spanish guides are live product modes over equivalent evidence semantics. Released-ref acceptance verifies distinct output paths, equal technical status/missing-required truth, and no cross-language overwrite.

evidence_retained.rationale: Release-plan, publication and released-ref real-public evidence are retained with artifact IDs and GitHub-computed SHA-256 digests; the permanent completion record captures their meaning and non-claims.

version_tag_or_release_published.rationale: Public non-draft/non-prerelease v0.9.1 was published on 2026-08-16 and independently verified to resolve exactly to reviewed source 082b41527f016058ff8c199b43beaca3e716c390.

known_limitations_documented.rationale: Local-only community-health scope, no GitHub server/API validation, no policy-content correctness, no good-first-issue availability check, no contributor trust/experience guarantee, no mutation and no WCAG/human multilingual acceptance claims are explicit.

contribution_and_issue_paths.rationale: General contribution guidance and a dedicated privacy-safe P-054 support/reproduction path exist on the public default branch.

canonical_handover_or_build_record_updat.rationale: The final completion record binds architecture, exact release source, v0.9.0 fail-honest history, v0.9.1 governed publication, released-ref acceptance, retained evidence, threat/privacy/accessibility review, limitations and recovery semantics.
